B017-01.notes: Row 2 of A (3,4) dot column 1 of B (2,1) = 6+4 = 10. Distractors: entry-wise products and wrong row/column.

B017-03.notes: (k-4)x = -10, so k = 4 gives 0 = -10, which has no solution.

flags: minor: many calculators return an error or a non-real value for (-64)^(2/3), but the standard algebra convention (cube root, then square) makes -64 valid, and {-64, 64} is the intended answer
B017-04.notes: (x^(1/3))^2 = 16, so x^(1/3) = ±4 and x = ±64. The trap is choosing {64} only.

B017-06.notes: 16 + 2(8+4+2) = 44. Common traps are counting each bounce only once (30) or adding an extra up-bounce.

flags: minor: the formula is given in generic a, b, C notation, so the student must map it to the sides here; that is fine

B017-08.notes: External common tangent length = sqrt(d^2 - (r1-r2)^2) = sqrt(100-4) = sqrt(96) = 4*sqrt(6). Distractor 6 comes from using r1+r2 (the internal tangent: sqrt(100-64) = 6). The setup requires drawing the right trapezoid.

B017-10.notes: Original: median 9, mean 9.4, range 11. New: median 9, mean 68/7 ≈ 9.71, range 19. Only the median is unchanged. The values 1 and 20 add 21, which is not 2*9.4 = 18.8, so the mean changes.
